text:
maria gonzalez: Heads up — noticed tail latency spikes in the obsv ingest pipeline after the new routing flip. 95p moved from ~120ms to ~400ms for traces. anyone else seeing this?

dan park: Yup. Bump lines up with the fanout change. Could be queue head-of-line or more cross-worker cache misses.

maria gonzalez: Thinking tradeoffs: fanout -> multiple workers per trace vs shared-queue + worker affinity. Fanout reduces per-worker state but increases fanout I/O.

kai chen: What do metrics say — processing time vs queueing? @infra-bot can you dump ingress queue depth and KV miss rate?

infra-bot: ingress-queue depth: 12 -> 80 in last 15m. avg proc_time: 230ms -> 370ms. p99 proc: 1.2s. kv_miss_rate: 8% -> 26%. dash: http://obsdash.local/ingest/queues

sasha ivanov: We also rolled the enrich change that changed the cache key normalization. miss rate jump aligns with that. more remote fetches explain extra latency.

dan park: Options: 1) backpressure / rate tokens, 2) shared queue with smarter batching, 3) sticky-routing to keep cache locality. Tradeoffs: batching lowers per-token cost but increases tail latency; sticky helps hits but risks hotspotting.

maria gonzalez: I prototyped a sticky-routing config that maps trace_id -> worker (consistent-hash). Small snippet: 

```
ingest.routing:
  mode: sticky
  shard_count: 64
  rebalance_interval: 10m
```

In lab this dropped kv miss to ~10% and p95 back to ~130ms. But hotspot risk is real.

kai chen: Hotspot mitigations: virtual shards + overflow fallback, or ring-resize with weighted shards. Need graceful rebalance to avoid thundering replays.

sasha ivanov: Also need to consider cost attribution: sticky routing changes resource patterns per shard which will make per-route cost noisy. We should expose per-shard (or per-virtual-shard) cost metrics.

dan park: +1. Next steps: (a) canary sticky-routing in low-traffic region, (b) add probes for kv_miss, queue_depth, p99, (c) add cost-latency dashboard to track regression.

maria gonzalez: I'll open a follow-up RFC with bench numbers, config, and runbook. assigning @kai chen to run canary, @dan park to own dashboard. keeping notes here.

kai chen: On it. I'll add a rolling-rebalance script to infra playbooks and a small executor to drain hot shards.

deploybot: canary created for cluster ingest-eu-2 with policy sticky shard_count=64. run id: deploy-2026-03-20-1

maria gonzalez: Thanks — if p99 returns to baseline we'll widen rollout. if spike persists revert to shared-queue + scale-out.

kai chen: I'll post a short playbook for rollback steps in the RFC thread once canary starts.

infra-bot: note: alert rule "ingest_queue_p99 > 800ms" triggered 3x in last 20m.

maria gonzalez: Good call. I'll keep monitoring and post updates. :thumbsup:
